business_scope.primary_industry_name: Airport Bonded In-Flight Meal Production and Direct Ramp Delivery

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law statutory corporate law with Delaware-style Business Corporations Act jurisprudence, Marshallese customary law, and Compact of Free Association federal framework)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No standalone bilateral investment treaty or comprehensive double taxation agreement is in force as of the effective date.

Compact of Free Association between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States (1986, as amended 2003), providing investment, establishment, and non-discrimination protections for U.S. nationals.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act 1990 (BCA), 14 MIRC Chapter 8, as amended; Non-Resident Domestic Corporations Regulations and Beneficial Ownership Record-Keeping Regulations; Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Act 2022 (AML/CFT Act); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2022; RMI Banking Commission AML/CFT Rulebook and Beneficial Ownership Guidance (2023); National Offshore Banking Act 1992.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories, and in-flight catering counterparties must be screened pre-incorporation and on an ongoing basis against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and RMI Financial Intelligence Unit domestic designations. PEP status, family-member/close-associate status, adverse media, source of wealth, and source of funds must be verified; any PEP or sanctions hit requires enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and if unresolved, rejection or mandatory divestment. Records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (RMI) Online Filing Portal (MI-CORP eRegistry), Majuro
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registry language is English; Marshallese and foreign-language names must be rendered in Latin-script transliteration with a notarized translation if non-English. The selected name must be distinguishable in the RMI corporate index and must contain a statutory corporate suffix: 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', or 'Ltd.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name expires after 30 days and may be extended once by filing an extension request before expiration; failure to extend or incorporate releases the name. If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file, within 30 days of the notice, a written appeal with the Registrar stating the distinctive elements and any third-party consent or license; the Registrar shall issue a reasoned response. A further judicial appeal may be docketed in the Civil Action Division of the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands under the BCA, or the applicant may resubmit an amended distinguishable name within 7 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or remote administrative address is permissible for non-resident Business Corporation customer-communications purposes, but the BCA statutory registered office must be a physical street address in the Marshall Islands maintained by a licensed RMI registered agent; a virtual office cannot satisfy this mandate. For the inflight catering scope, no RMI operating premises are required if kitchen operations are outside the RMI; if the kitchen or ramp unit is hosted at an RMI airport facility, a physical concession office and airport-issued security clearance are mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a pure non-resident contract-holding and procurement BC with no RMI premises, the annual likelihood of unannounced physical inspection is low (approximately 5%). The likelihood rises to 35-45% if the entity operates a bonded inflight kitchen or ramp delivery unit at a Marshall Islands airport, where customs, public health, and airport concession regulators conduct unannounced audits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act 1990, as amended (Republic of the Marshall Islands), particularly Sections 14 (Articles of Incorporation), 19 (Registered Office), 20 (Registered Agent), and 34 (Directors and Officers); supplemental Regulations under the Registrar of Corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro), acting through licensed Marshall Islands registered agents for non-resident filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Business Corporation statutory form, BCA Section 14).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Business Corporation; shares may be par-value or no-par value and issued for consideration fixed by the Board; no escrow account requirement under the BCA; non-resident corporations must maintain a licensed registered agent and registered office in the Marshall Islands.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that this Corporation adopt and ratify the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations, and that the incorporators' share subscriptions be accepted for the initial authorized capital, with paid-up capital being fully reflected by issuance of non-assessable common shares for lawful consideration; and RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be maintained at the address of the Corporation's licensed registered agent in the Marshall Islands, and that such registered agent be retained; and RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors and officers listed in the attached Schedule are elected, with the Managing Officer authorized to open bank accounts and execute all airport concession, food establishment, and environmental permit applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, via online portal or licensed registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability search for the proposed corporate name, including the mandatory distinguishing word 'Corporation,' 'Incorporated,' 'Company,' or 'Limited' or abbreviation. Upon availability, file a name reservation request and pay the reservation fee; hold the reservation pending submission of the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with corporate suffix
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for ambiguity or conflict, file an alternative name reservation or submit a written consent from the prior registered owner of the conflicting name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators, notary public, and licensed Marshall Islands resident registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation setting forth the corporate name, authorized capital and share structure, registered agent acceptance, registered office address, and statement of liability limitation. Each incorporator must sign, and signatures must be notarized or acknowledged before a notary public or authorized consular/embassy officer.
required_dossiers: Notarial certificate of acknowledgment for each incorporator
Written consent of the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns a deficiency notice, amend the deficient articles, re-execute with corrected information, and resubmit with the resubmission fee; failure to cure within 90 days voids the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, RMI; payment to the Government of the Marshall Islands.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Articles of Incorporation together with the statutory filing fee (USD 250) and any registered agent service fee. The Registrar stamps the filing date, assigns a corporate file number, and commences the statutory review for conformity with the BCA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, provide a written explanation of any defective provision or file an amendment under BCA Section 25; expedited review is available upon payment of the urgent processing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Confirmation of Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation; the registered office and registered agent are confirmed on the public register. The company is now duly incorporated and vested with separate legal personality; the company may obtain certified copies of the charter documents for banking and licensing purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is delayed or contains errors, submit a written request for correction or issuance of a certified replacement certificate; no negative inference attaches if the underlying filing is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, Adoption of Bylaws, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Business Corporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or execute a unanimous written consent. Adopt bylaws, ratify the share subscription and initial share issuance, appoint Directors and Officers, approve the banking resolution, and authorize execution of the catering concession and regulatory permits. Maintain signed minutes in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Waiver of notice or unanimous written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If minutes are challenged, cure by a subsequent Board ratification resolution; unanimous written consent may replace a physical meeting and remedy procedural defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Business License and Sector Licence Applications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Finance (Business License Division), Ministry of Health and Human Services (Environmental Health Unit), and Majuro International Airport Authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the national business license application, food establishment permit application for the in-flight catering kitchen, and the airport concession/access licence application for direct ramp delivery. Coordinate with the Environmental Protection Authority on environmental registration and with the Fire Department on premises clearance. All licences must be issued before catering production and ramp delivery commence.
required_dossiers: Food establishment permit application and food safety plan
Airport concession application and insurance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a license application is rejected, correct noted deficiencies, pay the resubmission fee, and reapply; appeal an adverse licensing decision to the relevant Ministry within 30 days, or request an interim operating permit pending inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health and Human Services (Environmental Health Unit) in coordination with the Majuro International Airport Authority, Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority, and Majuro Fire and Rescue Department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Establishment Permit for In-Flight Catering Kitchen and Airport Concession License for Direct Ramp Delivery Operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) under the Environmental Protection Act 1984 and its implementing regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Registration with Preliminary Environmental Assessment; full Environmental Impact Assessment (Category 1) is required only if the facility discharges more than 20,000 litres per day of treated effluent or undertakes on-site waste incineration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero discharge to lagoon waters unless a valid EPA discharge permit is held; wastewater pre-treatment must achieve TSS not exceeding 50 mg/L, BOD5 not exceeding 50 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 15 mg/L, and pH 6-9; solid food waste must be handled by an EPA-licensed waste carrier; VOC and solvent emissions limited to food-grade cleaning agents with no ozone-depleting substances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Majuro Fire and Rescue Department, including kitchen range suppression system, extinguisher placement, and exit compliance; structural load inspection certificate from the Ministry of Works, Infrastructure, and Utilities for kitchen equipment and generator installations; occupational health and food handler medical clearance for all catering personnel under the communicable disease control regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Ministry of Finance, Revenue and Taxation Office (RTO), Majuro — responsible for TIN issuance, Business Privilege Tax (BPT), and Income Tax Act 1989 administration. RMI Customs Service under the Ministry of Finance administers import duties, bonded warehouses, and export/aircraft-stores documentation. The Registrar of Corporations under the Office of the Attorney General handles corporate registration. No unified national e-portal exists for all taxes; BPT and income tax filings are submitted in paper or PDF to the RTO, while customs declarations are lodged electronically via the RMI customs clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate a Business Corporation under the Business Corporations Act 1996 through a licensed Registered Agent; obtain Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing — no minimum capital requirement applies to a non-resident-owned BC. Step 2: If the in-flight catering kitchen conducts activity inside RMI (a customs-bonded production plant at an airport), signatory officers must register the BC with the RTO within 30 days of commencing business to obtain a TIN and the combined BPT/Business License registration; a Foreign Investment Business License from the Ministry of Commerce is also required for foreign-owned entities. Step 3: Apply separately to RMI Customs for a bonded-factory/warehouse license and an importer–exporter code authorizing duty-suspended intake of raw food, beverages, and disposable service ware. Step 4: Register with the RMI Social Security Administration as an employer only when hiring locally covered employees (employer levy 6% of covered wages, employee levy 6%). Step 5: A purely passive non-resident BC with no RMI-source activity and no physical RMI presence need not appear on the RTO tax roll; upon request, the RTO will issue a certificate of non-registration or tax-exempt status letter for airline-contract counterparties and banking due diligence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the RMI treats a foreign-owned Business Corporation as a non-resident domestic corporation under a territorial exemption model. Taxable only on income sourced within RMI; all foreign-source income, including proceeds from meals sold to international air carriers where title and risk pass outside RMI territory or on board aircraft beyond RMI airspace, is exempt from income tax. No capital gains tax, no net-worth tax, no franchise tax, and no withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents. The only material RMI levy on an operating kitchen is BPT on gross receipts derived from RMI-source business activity, at 2% generally or 3.5% for wholesale distribution of goods, subject to the export exemption described below.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: RMI law has no check-the-box or US-style entity classification election and no OECD hybrid-mismatch election. The elections that are available include: (i) election of non-resident domestic corporation status via Articles of Incorporation and a 100% non-resident beneficial ownership certificate; (ii) fiscal-year election for income tax and BPT (calendar-year default, alternative fiscal year allowed by RTO); (iii) source-allocation election under title-passage and destination rules that places international flight catering revenue outside RMI-source income; (iv) customs bonded-warehouse election permitting duty suspension on inputs consumed in meals delivered to departing international flights; (v) election to claim the BPT export exemption on a quarterly return schedule. Group consolidation is not available; each BC files its own return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None — the RMI imposes no VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax at the national level. Transaction-based levies are limited to (a) Business Privilege Tax, a gross-receipts tax on persons engaged in business in RMI at 2% for most activities and 3.5% for wholesale distribution; (b) customs import duties on goods entering RMI; and (c) specific excise taxes on fuel and certain products. The in-flight catering kitchen is exposed primarily to customs import duty (suspended while operating within the bonded regime) and BPT on any domestic ramp-side sales to local carriers or ground retail.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT/GST registration threshold exists because no VAT/GST regime exists. BPT registration and the annual business-license obligation apply to any person engaged in business in RMI; the Business Privilege Tax Act 1988 contains a small-trader exemption for de minimis gross revenue, the exact current threshold of which should be confirmed with the RTO when the kitchen commences operations. The functional currency is the US dollar; the RMI has no central bank and adopts USD as legal tender.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction-control mandate applies. Invoices and BPT records may be kept in paper or PDF and must be retained for at least 5 years. The only mandatory digital interface is customs: RMI Customs processes bonded-warehouse entries, import declarations, and export/aircraft-stores clearances through an electronic declaration system requiring API or portal filing of manifest data. A bonded catering kitchen must maintain an electronic inventory ledger reconciling all meals produced, aircraft delivery receipts, and duty-suspended inputs, which must be available to customs officers on demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: No VAT/GST zero-rating exists. Export relief is instead secured through three parallel rules: (i) Income Tax source rule — gross revenue from meals supplied to foreign airlines for consumption on international segments is treated as foreign-source income when title and risk pass outside RMI or at the aircraft door, and is therefore exempt from RMI income tax; (ii) BPT export exemption — gross receipts from goods sold or delivered for export, including bonded airline catering loaded on departing international flights, are excluded from taxable gross revenue; (iii) Customs aircraft-stores relief — food, beverages, and disposables that leave RMI with the aircraft are free of import duty despite having entered under bond, provided the bonded warehouse permit, production records, and the aircraft exit manifest reconcile exactly.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration or Aircraft Stores (Supplies) exit manifest per flight
Bill of Lading or Master Air Waybill covering each catering delivery
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank MT103/SWIFT evidencing settlement from the airline
Catering delivery docket and flight-number reconciliation ledger
Bonded warehouse permit and goods-received/goods-issued inventory registers
Quarterly BPT export-exemption schedule filed with the RTO
HACCP/ISO 22000 hygiene certification evidence retained for food-safety and export-eligibility audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The RTO and RMI Customs cross-match BPT returns, customs manifests, and banking inflows for catering operations. An unsubstantiated export-exemption claim triggers: (i) reassessment of BPT at the full applicable rate of 2% to 3.5% on the disallowed gross revenue; (ii) interest accrual at 0.75% per month; (iii) a 25% civil penalty of the understated gross revenue where the error is attributable to negligence; (iv) criminal liability under the Income Tax Act 1989 and Customs Act for false export or aircraft-stores declarations, punishable by fines up to USD 10,000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 years; and (v) for customs fraud, forfeiture of goods, revocation of the bonded license, disgorgement of avoided duty, and a civil penalty equal to twice the duty evaded.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, operating under the Ministry of Finance and the Marshall Islands Banking Act 1984; the Marshall Islands does not maintain a separate central bank or a domestic currency issuance authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The legal tender of the Marshall Islands is the United States Dollar (USD). There is no foreign exchange control law, no capital account restriction, and no current account restriction imposed by the Marshall Islands Government. Both current account transactions (trade and service payments) and capital account transactions (foreign direct investment, equity injections, loans, and profit repatriation) are freely convertible within the limits of the local banking system's correspondent banking relationships. Profit remittance of a non-resident Business Corporation is legally permitted, subject to the entity maintaining good standing under the Business Corporations Act, possessing a valid Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) if engaged in a foreign investment activity, and satisfying the anti-money laundering and source-of-funds verification requirements of the local settlement bank. Practical hurdles are primarily bank-level correspondent banking compliance and documentary diligence rather than statutory currency controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no export proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory timeline within which aviation catering export receipts must be repatriated or exchanged. Since the domestic currency is USD and all export receipts are naturally denominated in USD, the requirement to sell export proceeds to a central bank or designated agent is not applicable. Corporate treasury may retain export earnings offshore in the entity's designated settlement account without conversion obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Marshall Islands (BOMI), Majuro Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for in-bound aviation contract wire settlements and monthly ACH disbursements

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam, Marshall Islands Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and secondary clearing account for cross-border wire transfers

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW. Offshore digital financial institutions and electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not eligible to hold a banking license in the Marshall Islands and are not recognized as domestic settlement banks under the Banking Act 1984. Use of an unlicensed offshore EMI for the receiving of capital injections or trade settlement is legally risky and likely to trigger foreign exchange compliance rejections by the local banking system. An EMI may serve only as an ancillary payment aggregation tool when cleared onward through a licensed correspondent bank, but it must not be used as the primary treasury holding account or cross-border clearing rail for the licensed inflight catering operation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident Business Corporation, the Marshall Islands Banking Commissioner does not prescribe a statutory universal physical presence rule. Local commercial banks generally permit remote account opening using apostilled and legalized corporate documents, notarized board resolutions, a certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation, and a foreign investment business license. However, in practice the bank's compliance officer or the correspondent US bank may require at least one director or the authorized signatory to attend an in-person interview at the Majuro or Guam branch before final activation of high-value disbursement functionality. Video-based KYC interviews may be accepted for initial onboarding, but digital final signing is not guaranteed. Treasury documentation should plan for a physical attestation visit by the principal authorized officer or, alternatively, appointment of a local resident director/professional signatory to satisfy physical presence requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt business corporation with no physical operating footprint in the Marshall Islands
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing; certified Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws; registered agent certificate; Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL); notarized board resolution appointing signatories; detailed ownership and beneficial ownership chart with passport copies; local supply contract from the airport concession or in-flight catering facility if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk aviation supply chain involving cross-border food imports and international invoice payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, purchase orders, customs broker engagement, Import/Export Business License, contract with airline carriers and catering facility operators, enterprise resource planning records supporting the operational cash cycle, and internal AML/CFT policies if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual use of a capital escrow account for frequent high-volume monthly disbursements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy statement, projected settlement schedule, counterparty due-diligence files for recurring vendors, source-of-funds evidence from parent company or beneficial owner, audited financial statements or accountant's letter confirming the nature of the transaction flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporation attempting to open an account with locally licensed bank but without local directorship presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Engagement of a registered Marshall Islands corporate agent; appointment of a local resident director or licensed registered agent as co-signatory; signed trust and company service provider declaration; original certified copies of passport and proof of address for all beneficial owners.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for capital injection requires an international SWIFT MT103 wire denominated in USD from the parent or shareholder to the Marshall Islands licensed commercial bank. The beneficiary must be identified by full legal name, bank account number, and the bank's correspondent ABA/routing chain. When initiating the wire, the sending institution must include a clear transaction description, such as 'Capital contribution to MH_BC under Business Corporations Act', and reference the bank-approved entity identification number and the Foreign Investment Business License number. For the purposes of the US-based correspondent clearing system, the wire should be annotated with an ISO 20022 purpose code consistent with an equity capital injection where the system requires it, but because the Marshall Islands imposes no foreign exchange approval, the bank-level beneficial interest verification and the source of funds statement are the decisive controls. The receiving bank should issue a credit confirmation and a deposit receipt to the treasury department for audit trail integrity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements to international airline suppliers, food processors, packaging vendors, and fuel or logistics partners are executed through direct SWIFT MT103 credit transfers or documentary commercial letters of credit (LC) where the transaction requires guaranteed payment. For low-frequency high-value aviation catering production equipment and bulk commodity purchases, an irrevocable confirmed letter of credit opened by the Marshall Islands bank or a US correspondent bank is recommended. For recurring invoices, monthly USD ACH transfers can be settled through the local bank to domestic suppliers or through the US automated clearing house network if the beneficiary is a US institution. All wires and LCs must identify the underlying trade invoice number, the ISIC 5621 catering service contract, and the airway bill or delivery confirmation. Payment execution must be aligned with the bank's sanctions screening, OFAC list verification, and the food import compliance documentation for the destination jurisdiction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD forward contracts with a licensed US correspondent bank for the cover of euro, yen, and Australian dollar supply-chain liabilities

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted outside the Marshall Islands banking system in regulated US or Asian financial centers, back-to-back with the monthly EBITDA exposure of the inflight catering kitchen
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) used only when accompanied by a matching project finance or capital lease obligation for aircraft catering facility construction
Currency options purchased from an approved international bank, strictly for the mitigation of adverse foreign exchange movements in the purchase of imported frozen and fresh raw materials

FX swaps and sale and repurchase structures using the USD as primary settlement currency, limited to counterparties that are eligible under the bank's internal derivatives policy and the Marshalls' regulatory standards for institutional non-retail clients

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Annual Franchise Maintenance Fee (Business Corporations Act, Section 106)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Corporate Registry, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (lodged through the licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing due within the calendar month of the anniversary of incorporation; no fixed calendar-year due date. Example: incorporation on 15 March requires filing by 31 March each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 200 assessed immediately upon late submission; unpaid fees accrue for a maximum of 12 months, after which the Registrar may administratively strike off the corporation without court order; reinstatement requires payment of all arrears, penalties, and a reinstatement fee of approximately USD 300.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Annual Confirmation (AML/CFT Compliance under the Commercial and Corporate Registered Agents Rules 2018)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent in the Marshall Islands as statutory custodian of the confidentiality-protected UBO register; records subject to lawful inspection by the Financial Intelligence Support Unit (FISU)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary of incorporation, and as a supplemental update within 14 days of any share transfer, allotment, or change in beneficial ownership of 10% or more of shares or voting rights.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to provide accurate UBO data obliges the registered agent to report the entity to FISU; a false UBO entry is a regulatory offense and may cause the agent to resign, triggering involuntary strike-off; continued non-compliance may lead to revocation of the agent's license affecting all client entities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Internal Statutory Register Audit and Secretary's Certificate of Records Location
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and corporate secretary (internal document retained with the statutory minute book; no filing with the Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the annual meeting, and in any event within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; the certificate of records location must be refreshed whenever the physical records address changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A defective register found during Registrar inspection constitutes a breach of BCCA Section 105 (books and records); directors and officers may be held personally liable for damages caused by inaccurate share registers or missing minute entries.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for a private, non-listed Marshall Islands Business Corporation. An audit may become mandatory only if (i) required by the articles of incorporation or bylaws, (ii) resolved by the board or shareholders, (iii) imposed by a lender, insurer, or aviation catering contract counterparty, or (iv) required by the host-country operating license for the airport catering kitchen. No public filing of audited financial statements is required in the Marshall Islands.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No Marshall Islands statutory GAAP is imposed on non-resident Business Corporations; management may adopt IFRS or US GAAP, with IFRS preferred for aviation-related cross-border operations. The accounting framework selected must be consistently applied and supported by underlying books and records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the RMI AML/CFT framework and the Commercial and Corporate Registered Agents Rules 2018, the licensed registered agent must maintain a confidential beneficial ownership register for the corporation. The corporation must confirm and refresh UBO data (any individual holding directly or indirectly 10% or more of shares, voting rights, or ultimate control) at least annually on the incorporation anniversary, and within 14 days of any share transfer. Confirmation is effected by a written UBO declaration signed by a director or officer and delivered to the registered agent; the register is not publicly accessible and is disclosed only to authorized RMI authorities on lawful demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share ledger and share transfer ledger)
Register of Mortgages and Charges (if any)
Register of Beneficial Owners (maintained confidentially by the licensed registered agent)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 1,400 per annum covering licensed registered agent, registered office in the Marshall Islands, statutory mail handling, annual report preparation, and UBO register administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 15,000 for a voluntary or counterparty-required IFRS/US GAAP audit of a mid-size airline inflight catering operation; not required under Marshall Islands law for a non-resident Business Corporation

approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
